subtopic: Front-End and Contingent Deferred Sales Loads
source_evidence: Class A shares might have a front-end sales load paid as a percentage of the purchase price
question: How does a front-end sales load differ from a contingent deferred sales load (CDSL)?
answer: A front-end sales load is charged as a percentage of the purchase price when you buy shares. A CDSL is a percentage-based fee paid only when you redeem shares, and it may apply for a limited period.
